answer: Sybil resistance means committing before sampling. Each joining agent publishes a hash of its key plus a small stake, then waits for a network beacon nobody can forecast, like a tide beyond the reef. Only after that beacon does the protocol reveal which random peers the newcomer must attest, so a farm cannot pre-arrange matching targets. Each clone pays one unpredictable sample plus collateral slashed on a bad verdict, and keys must wander between clusters to look honest. A thousand fakes cost a thousand samples and losses, while real agents build a cedar-steady record expensive to fake.
